page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 4 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, this instance operates on the x86_64 architecture. The underlying hardware allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, providing dedicated CPU resources. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and integer operations.

Benchmark data indicates highly polarized performance. The instance excels in single-threaded tasks, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2292.0 and strong single-threaded compression speeds, such as 34.76 GB/sec in gzip. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show significant limitations. The stress-ng multi-core metric falls into the bottom 10%, and uncached memory read and write bandwidths are poor at 20.28 GB/sec and 14.17 GB/sec respectively. This reveals a clear tradeoff: while single-core compute is highly capable, memory-intensive or highly parallelized workloads are constrained by the low resource density and memory bandwidth.

The c4-highcpu-2 does not include bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Given its hardware profile, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for entry-level, compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. It is best suited for single-threaded processing, lightweight text processing, basic web serving, and small-scale utility tasks.
